data.narrative:
Echodyne, a Series C-stage defense and security company, has raised $224M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies—Castelion ($13.0B), Stark Defence ($4.0B), and Neros ($2.5B)—alongside broader Defense & Security comparables including public names (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and later-stage private peers such as Anduril Industries and Helsing.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $224M raised proxy, yielding $381M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-stage Defense & Security comparables produces a $4.0B implied valuation, with a range spanning $2.5B to $13.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in market position and customer concentration within the defense tech sector at this stage.

The two methods produce a median triangulated valuation of $2.2B, with a low-end estimate of $324M (weighted toward stage-progression) and a high-end estimate of $4.6B (weighted toward peer multiples). Key uncertainties include Echodyne's relative position within the peer set on revenue scale, government customer concentration, and technology differentiation—factors not fully captured by stage alone and likely driving the substantial $2.3B range between low and high scenarios.
